cells.tense: You're here with it now — the thing you pictured is finished, and you're in the middle of setting it down.
cells.ask: Follow the pull that's actually yours today — the direction that comes from genuine engagement — and let it set the pace for what's next, giving you momentum that doesn't need pushing.
cells.core:
What you imagined has been lived all the way through, and that's why it satisfies. That's a real kind of fullness — content because the whole of it was felt, not because every last piece came out right.

The finishing is clean here. You hand the finished thing over, or set it on the shelf, and you already feel the next thing beginning to pull — not as pressure, just as the direction you'd head anyway. Finishing like this opens instead of closing. You have a natural rhythm for what comes next, and you can trust it to set the pace for you.
cells.sheetLine: What you imagined has been lived through, and that's the fullness.
cells.verb: imagining something fully until it's real to you, satisfied by the feeling of it rather than a count of what's done
cells.place: the step where finishing and starting are the same move — where something is complete enough to let go, and letting go is what opens what's next

cells.tense: You're already living past the finish line — bracing for what comes next before this thing has let you feel it.
cells.ask: Tend one thing that's actually growing — this one, at the pace it's really moving — and let the care be steady instead of urgent, giving you back the ease of holding without clutching.
cells.core:
You're dreaming ahead of what's been processed, so the completion you're after keeps moving out of reach. Pushing toward the next imagined version has replaced letting this one land, and the pushing itself is what keeps it from arriving.

Picture the other shape of this: the harvest gets brought in because the season was actually lived, and the next picture grows from ground you've walked. A finished thing wants to be something you set down. Let this one be done in your hands — not perfect, just complete — and the next picture starts growing from what you actually lived rather than from what you're afraid won't come.
cells.sheetLine: You're pushing past the finish to a version that hasn't landed yet.
cells.verb: imagining something fully until it's real to you, satisfied by the feeling of it rather than a count of what's done
cells.place: the step where finishing and starting are the same move — where something is complete enough to let go, and letting go is what opens what's next

cells.tense: You're standing just behind a finish you already crossed, and you haven't let yourself be on the other side.
cells.ask: Sit with one thing you know about what you made — let the knowing be quietly certain before you say anything about it — and let that honest perception be what carries you across.
cells.core:
There's a lot imagined and a lot felt, but the last step of letting it be complete hasn't been taken. So the satisfaction stays out of reach even though the work is there, waiting to be counted as done.

When the finishing is flowing, the end of a thing feels like the start of the next one. You finish, you know it finished, and you carry the knowing forward without needing to prove it. You already know how this one goes. Let what you know stand as true for a moment before you decide anything about it, and the finishing follows — you were already on the other side.
cells.sheetLine: The work is done and you're still standing at the edge of believing it.
cells.verb: imagining something fully until it's real to you, satisfied by the feeling of it rather than a count of what's done
cells.place: the step where finishing and starting are the same move — where something is complete enough to let go, and letting go is what opens what's next

cells.tense: You're already shaping what gets made next — but you talk about it like it's happening on its own.
cells.ask: Pick one distinction about what matters here — sharpen your attention to that one difference — and let the practice serve what's actually growing instead of your worry about it.
cells.core:
You're already integrating and completing things — deciding what's finished, what carries, what's next — and you're doing it as if the process runs itself. The choosing is running, and you haven't said so, so the decisions feel like they belong to the work rather than to you.

When this sits in your hands, careful attention is a pleasure. Time alone with the piece connects you to it rather than cutting you off, and refining it feeds the growth instead of your worry about whether it'll land. Name one choice as yours — the one you already made — and the practice stops running underneath you and starts working with you.
